transcript.label: Transcript turn 10 · admission time, as a blank chain
transcript.said: Pattern B is the better of the two, and less common than you’d think. Which makes the next one worth getting precise, because it’s what shows the pattern is actually landing: every admission runs through five steps, and the gap between the first and the last is your Admission TAT. The graphic has that chain with the times left blank. Fill in a typical day’s clock times and we’ll see exactly where the time goes.

text: Pattern B is the better of the two, and less common than you’d think.
That makes the next one worth getting exact. It shows whether the pattern is really landing.
Every admission runs through five steps. The gap between the first and the last is your admission time. Fill in a typical day’s clock times, and we’ll see where the time goes.
prompts: Arrival about 1 PM, in the bed by 4:30 PM
Our times change a lot from day to day
Do the times need to be exact?

blocks.title: Five steps, times left blank
blocks.deck: A typical day’s clock times are enough. They do not have to be exact.

stages.name: Patient arrives, or Emergency says admit
stages.what: The clock starts when the patient arrives, or when Emergency decides to admit.

stages.name: Paperwork done
stages.what: Registration and admission papers are complete.

stages.name: Bed given in the system
stages.what: A bed is put against the patient’s name in your hospital software.

stages.name: Ward or ICU confirms the bed is ready
stages.what: The ward or ICU says the bed is clean and ready to take the patient.

stages.name: Patient in the bed
stages.what: The patient is physically in the bed. The clock stops here.

blocks.caption: The gap between the first step and the last is your admission time.
